description:
The 2026-04-15 review identified a cluster of foundational issues in
the results explorer that share the same root cause: visualization
primitives are defined inline per component instead of shared. These
bugs produce inconsistent UX today and block clean follow-on work
(chart-coverage expansion, parity tests, comparison artifacts).

Five distinct problems, fixable as one coordinated change:

**Issue 1 - Dual definition of "speedup" on the Compare page.**
Summary cards (Compare.tsx:225) compute `slowest_primary / primary`
(a "vs slowest" spread). Per-query breakdown table (Compare.tsx:392)
computes `slowest / fastest` (within-query spread). Speedup chart
(NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:57) computes `baseline / this`
(per-baseline ratio). All three render with the same "x" label.
Users see contradictory numbers on the same page.

**Issue 2 - Color/style constants duplicated across 4 files.**
`COMPARE_COLORS` / `CHART_COLORS` (`["#3b82f6","#10b981","#f59e0b","#ef4444"]`)
defined in Compare.tsx:17, NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:22,
DivergingBarChart.tsx:11, QueryTimingChart.tsx:18. Plus magic numbers
`LOG2_MIN/MAX`, `MAX_DELTA_PCT=300`, `GRID_STOPS=[0.25,0.5,1,2,4]`
scattered without a single source.

**Issue 3 - "Failed to Decode Data" error is opaque and misleading.**
When a benchmark artifact is missing, Vite serves the SPA HTML
fallback (HTTP 200), `DecompressionStream` then throws
"Failed to Decode Data" (manifest.ts:81-87). Users see this on the
TPC-H Results page (the user's screenshot of 2026-04-15) when the
page loads before the manifest filter has resolved the phase.
Three sub-problems: (a) BenchmarkIndex.tsx:84 useEffect fires before
`phases` resolves; (b) error message gives no clue what happened;
(c) Vite SPA fallback is detected as "decode error" rather than 404.

**Issue 4 - SVG charts have hardcoded viewBox dimensions.**
NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:69 (`viewBox="0 0 600 …"`),
DivergingBarChart.tsx:91 (`viewBox="0 0 600 …"`),
QueryTimingChart.tsx:58 (`viewBox="0 0 800 …"`),
GroupedQueryChart (`viewBox="0 0 900 …"`). All use
`preserveAspectRatio="none"` so on wide screens text squishes and
bar widths look wrong. This is a primary visual contributor to the
user's "sub-par visualizations" complaint.

**Issue 5 - Compare uses `geomean_ms` ignoring per-benchmark primary metric.**
Compare.tsx:151-156 hardcodes `getPrimary(r) = r.geomean_ms`. For
benchmarks where `power_score` is the primary metric (defined in
RANKING_METRIC_BY_FAMILY), the speedup math runs on the wrong axis.
Already exposed via BenchmarkSummary.ranking.primary_metric for the
heatmap (QueryHeatmap.tsx:102-107) - Compare needs to consume the
same registry.

work_units.summary: Create `results-explorer/src/lib/chartTheme.ts` consolidating colors, scales, and chart constants

work_units.notes:
Soft cross-item dep: helpers live in `chartMath.ts`, created by
`explorer-establish-cli-explorer-parity-tests` w1 (declared as a
hard dep on this item). If for any reason this lands first,
create `chartMath.ts` here and let parity adopt it.


Two distinct concepts deserve two distinct names - but only TWO,
not THREE:

  - **`vsSlowestRatio(thisMs, slowestMs)`** - used by summary cards
    and breakdown table. Always `>= 1`. Labelled "vs slowest" in UI.
    Replaces both the dual definitions in Compare.tsx:225 and :392.

  - **`vsBaselineRatio(thisMs, baselineMs)`** - used by
    NormalizedSpeedupChart only. Can be < 1 or > 1. Labelled
    "vs <baseline name>" in UI.

UI labels MUST always include the comparison target so users
cannot read "1.5x" without knowing what it is relative to.

Both functions live in `chartMath.ts` (created by
`explorer-establish-cli-explorer-parity-tests` w1) when it lands
first; if this item lands first, create them here and let the
parity item adopt them.
work_units.summary: Unify the speedup definition: pick `slowest / this` for cross-result, `baseline / this` for per-baseline; rename so the contract is visible in the API

work_units.notes:
Pattern: switch from `viewBox="0 0 600 H"` + `preserveAspectRatio="none"`
to a measured layout:
  - `useElementSize` returns `{ width, height }` from a ref;
    internal ResizeObserver, debounced via rAF if needed
  - Caller sets `viewBox="0 0 ${width} ${H}"`
  - Drop `preserveAspectRatio="none"` so text and bar widths scale
    consistently
  - Honor min-width with horizontal scroll fallback for mobile

Convert NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx as the reference implementation.
Add a Vitest test that mounts the chart at three widths
(400, 800, 1600) and asserts the SVG `viewBox` width attribute
matches the container width (snapshot SVG attrs, not pixels).
work_units.summary: Build `lib/useElementSize.ts` ResizeObserver hook and convert NormalizedSpeedupChart as the proof of concept

work_units.notes:
Single function: `primaryMetricFor(benchmark: string): "power_score" | "geomean_ms"`.
Source of truth remains Python (`benchbox/core/ranking.py` -
RANKING_METRIC_BY_FAMILY). Comment in `ranking.ts` MUST cite the
canonical Python file path so the mirror cannot drift silently.

Add a parity fixture (or unit test) that pins the registry
contents on both sides - divergence fails CI.

Touch-up pass after the foundational changes:
  - QueryHeatmap.tsx:93-99 - wrap `colMins` in `useMemo` keyed on
    `summary` (the `for` loop runs every render today; it spreads
    across `query_ids.length × platforms.length`)
  - DivergingBarChart.tsx:73-79 (`sorted`, `medianDelta`) - also
    `useMemo` if the chart re-renders on baseline change

Each memoization must be measured with a quick perf check (browser
profiler on a 100-platform × 99-query case) and only kept if it
changes render time meaningfully - do not pile on memoization for
its own sake.
